messages.content: What is the dominant genetic trait of a Lion?

message.content: In domestic cats and many other mammals, the presence of a mane (the long, shaggy hair around the head and neck) is controlled by a dominant allele. In lions, the same principle applies: the allele that codes for mane growth is dominant over the allele that results in a smooth coat. Thus, if a lion inherits at least one copy of the mane‑coding allele from either parent, it will develop a mane (in males). This makes the mane a classic example of a dominant genetic trait in lions.
